target_customer: Franchise and multi-unit restaurant and retail operators hiring hourly staff
problem: Hourly hiring was slow and paper based; the founder hired high schoolers with thin resumes as a franchisee and wanted a faster mobile process.
business_model: B2B SaaS monthly subscription per location
product_category: Applicant tracking and onboarding software for hourly work

founders.name: Rob Hunter
education: Ivey Business School (connection per YC page, degree not stated)
founders.background_notes: Per YC page and YC blog; bankrupt at 29 per YC page

technical_complexity.rationale: Mobile first applicant tracking with text to apply and scheduling was standard web engineering in 2015.

defensibility.rationale: Workflow software for franchisees was copyable; stickiness came from franchise brand relationships and integrations.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing what incumbents did around 2015; later vendor pages show HigherMe integrating with Snagajob rather than competing head on.

market_need_then: Founder experienced the pain directly as a franchisee; YC blog from March 2015 frames resumes as a poor signal for first jobs. No independent demand data found.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand found; name is a pun on hire and higher. Vendor pages show a mature product brand but no independent brand evidence.

outcome_analysis: HigherMe built hiring software around a former franchisee founder's lived pain and grew to a reported 20,000 locations by its own claim, then was acquired. The acquirer and date could not be confirmed from primary sources, so the reasons for the exit and its price are unknown. Success looks like founder market fit in a niche vertical with steady subscription revenue.
notes: Acquirer unverified: one aggregator (SeedTable) names Hunter Search Capital with a 2021-01-01 date that may be a placeholder; no press release found, so exit acquirer and date left null. YC page says acquisition at age 36 for Rob Hunter. A $1.5M seed in 2016-10 (YC, Barbara Corcoran Venture Partners, angels) appears only in aggregators (SeedTable, StartupIntros, ZoomInfo) and totals vary ($1.6M to $2.44M), so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. No dated 2015 competitor sources found; the competitor search returned only 2026 vendor listicles. Location conflicts (Toronto per YC, Boston per 43North).
